title: Marbled fondant
subtitle: two or more colours of fondant folded together to create a veined effect
excerpt: Marbled fondant is a decorating method where two or more colours of fondant are folded together and rolled out so the colours run through the surface in distinct veins. The key is to stop folding before the colours blend fully together. Overworked fondant turns a flat intermediate colour; the right amount of folding gives clear, clean veins.
sourceNotes: Marbled fondant technique documented in British sugar-craft and cake-decorating manuals from the 1980s onward. Marbling of edible sugar pastes follows the same principle as marbling in other decorative crafts.

glossaryTerms.definition: A pliable sugar paste made from icing sugar, glucose, and gelatine that can be rolled thin and draped over a cake to give a smooth finish. Also known as sugarpaste.

content.text: Marbled fondant is made by folding two colours of

together until they form a veined pattern, then rolling the piece out to cover a cake. The number of folds determines the result: too few and the colours sit in separate chunks, too many and they blend to a single colour.
Classic marble uses white and one other colour. Using three colours gives a richer effect but is harder to control. For a first attempt, keep it to two.
Knead each colour of fondant separately until soft and pliable. Divide so that the main colour makes up about two thirds of the total and the accent colour makes up one third.
Roll each piece into a rough log. Lay the accent colour log on top of the main colour log and press them together along their length.

Fold the combined piece in half, then twist the two ends in opposite directions 3 to 4 turns. Fold in half again and press together. At this stage the colours should be running through each other in thick veins.

Stop folding and place the piece on a surface lightly dusted with icing sugar. Roll out gently to 4 mm thick, turning the piece a quarter turn after each roll to keep the veins from aligning in one direction only.
Drape over the cake and smooth down as usual. Cut the excess away at the base with a sharp knife.

attrs.problem: Colours blending to a single muddy colour
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-twisting and over-folding; each additional fold blends the colours further together.
attrs.fix: Limit the process to 3 to 4 twists and 2 folds. Stop as soon as you can see distinct veins running through the piece.

attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling out with repeated strokes in the same direction; this aligns the veins and can flatten or erase them.
attrs.fix: Turn the piece 90 degrees after every 2 or 3 rolls. If veins have disappeared, fold the rolled piece once, press together, and roll again.

attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling cold or stiff fondant; it tears rather than stretching smoothly.
attrs.fix: Knead both pieces until they are warm and soft before starting. If the fondant is cracking, work in a tiny amount of white vegetable fat with your hands.
